newsitem.title: UK: IPE may use quarters to extend Brent to 30 months.
newsitem.headline: IPE may use quarters to extend Brent to 30 months.

text.p: London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) may adopt a quarterly system, trading one month in each quarter on forward periods, when it extends its flagship Brent crude futures contract to 30 months forward, said a spokesman for the exchange on Monday.
"One possible method might be to run 12 consecutive months as is currently the case and then quarterly contract months extending out a further year and a half," he said.

The IPE Brent contract currently trades the 12 months from February 1997 out to January 1998. If such a quarterly system was introduced now the extra contracts traded would be March 1998, June 1998, September 1998, December 1998, March 1999 and June 1999.

"This type of quarterly maturity cycle is consistent with other financial futures markets," the spokesman added. "The market seems to be inclined towards a simple structure whereby quarterly months become relevent consecutive months at the appropriate time.
"The untraded months between the quarterly months would simply be added to the board following each expiry".
The spokesman said the exchange was still in the process of consulting the oil industry about ways to extend the contract but "we expect to have proposals in place by IP week."
The Institute of Petroleum week of industry functions will be held in London during the week beginning February 17.
